newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish debt - new regional financing law.
newsitem.headline: Spanish debt - new regional financing law.

text.p: Since 1978, Spain has been moving toward greater fiscal autonomy in its 17 regional governments. During an initial period, regional governments were responsible only for expenditures, but they are now gaining some control over a part of income tax.

Under the system introduced at the end of September, each regional government will receive up to 30 percent of all income tax and will have the possibility of changing tax rates by up to a maximum of 20 percent on this income tax segment.

Of every 100 pesetas paid by an individual in income tax, the regional government will receive 30 pesetas --for one year, 1997, just 15 -- and it will have the power to reduce or increase this tax by 20 percent, in other words by about six pesetas.

Two of the 17 regions, the Basque Country and Navarra, have a higher degree of fiscal autonomy for historical reasons and therefore still have a different regulatory framework. Other regions have said there too were interested in this greater degree of autonomy.
Under the new law, a system to transfer funds to the poorest regions has been set-up, but critics call the plan inadequate, saying huge regional wealth diifferences could emerge.
